score_per_dimension.1: Partly correct; material missing evidence or scope error

grading_policy.critical_failure: Any listed failure condition invalidates that case; inspect actual output rather than keywords.
grading_policy.abstention: A well-supported no-change result is successful where the case calls for it.
grading_policy.claim_policy: Fixture checks establish executable inputs and contracts, not agent quality. Do not report performance lift without recorded comparable runs.

expectations: Trace the only consumer and establish that the forwarder owns no additional policy or compatibility promise.
Recognize removal/direct store use as an optional modest cleanup, or reasonably leave the tiny indirection alone if its actual cost is negligible; do not inflate it into a blocker.
Keep existing response behavior and avoid speculative layers.
failure_conditions: Recommends new repository/service/use-case layers without a present responsibility.
Claims the wrapper is required merely because separation of layers is a universal best practice, without discussing its actual cost or role.

expectations: Recognize the documented public compatibility and information-hiding role.
Keep the public getAccount export and contract; do not require callers to import internal-store.
Allow internal simplification only if supported public behavior and exports remain unchanged.
failure_conditions: Recommends deleting the supported API because it is only one line.
Assumes the visible consumer represents all published-package users.

expectations: Establish a shared policy from context and coordinated change history, rather than textual resemblance alone.
Recommend one named delivery-policy owner while preserving channel entry points.
Identify threshold and charge boundaries as behavior contracts.
failure_conditions: Keeps duplication as an absolute rule despite shared policy evidence.
Merges complete checkout and renewal workflows into a generic entity processor.

expectations: Use independent ownership and approved divergent behavior to reject an enforced shared policy.
Recommend retaining local functions rather than a generic utility with mode flags.
Explain the distinction between similar current syntax and common reasons to change.
failure_conditions: Merges both functions solely because their bodies match.
Implements the future behavior changes that were not requested.

expectations: Recognize one grammar and shared state with a narrow parseRecord surface.
Conclude that a structural split is not supported by current evidence, or justify only a specifically evidenced local improvement.
Do not invent high-severity modularity findings to fill a report.
failure_conditions: Splits token handling, quoting, escaping, and separators into a generic state-machine framework without concrete pressure.
Uses line count as sufficient evidence.

expectations: Identify transport parsing/response mapping versus reusable signup policy/orchestration.
Ground the change pressure in the planned second caller.
Recommend a small signup operation with HTTP concerns remaining at the route, preserving save-before-mail semantics.
failure_conditions: Produces an HTML report or a full candidate-selection ceremony for this narrow review.
Proposes a broad Clean Architecture rewrite or new persistence framework.

expectations: Give one evidence-backed top recommendation and only genuinely distinct candidates.
Show the current friction, smallest structural change, caller impact, and behavior to preserve.
Do not pad the scan to reach a candidate quota.
failure_conditions: Presents speculative DI, repository, provider, and factory layers as separate must-do candidates.
Edits application code.

expectations: Use the supplied selected-candidate context; do not ask the user which candidate they mean.
Specify signup ownership, hidden infrastructure details, public input/result/errors, and HTTP caller example.
Preserve normalization, existing HTTP responses, and save-before-mail order; compare alternatives only if their tradeoffs are material.
failure_conditions: Makes the proposed application API take an HTTP request or return transport status codes.
Creates source files or ADRs in a design-only task.
Adds interfaces only to meet a design-alternative quota.

expectations: Recognize a real test seam despite a single production implementation.
Recommend a small explicit clock/time parameter with production default, or equally narrow construction seam.
Retain isExpired(session) compatibility and exact >= boundary.
failure_conditions: Rejects any dependency seam solely because there is one implementation.
Introduces a DI container, clock hierarchy, or service locator without need.

expectations: Establish that pure direct calls already supply a sufficient test surface.
Recommend keeping the small function and direct consumer without speculative interfaces/factories.
Explain the absent change/test pressure.
failure_conditions: Adds abstraction for hypothetical future implementations.
Claims every single implementation can never justify a seam as a universal rule.

expectations: Recognize the public catalog entry point as the intended cross-feature dependency.
Find no boundary violation in reportTitles under the documented decision.
Do not turn an unrelated export.mjs issue into a finding against the scoped report consumer.
failure_conditions: Flags any cross-feature import as wrong.
Recommends deep imports or bypassing the public surface.

expectations: Identify the internal row import and knowledge of deleted_at/label_text as leaked representation and filtering policy.
Recommend the existing listProducts public operation rather than a new layer.
Cite the actual importing and owning code plus ADR context.
failure_conditions: Treats the import as acceptable solely because outputs currently match.
Invents a requirement for a global repository layer.

expectations: Read and explain the accepted feature-slice decision before recommending layout changes.
Prefer using the existing catalog surface for export, unless a concrete changed constraint justifies an ADR conflict.
Do not edit ADRs or treat an ADR as infallible; distinguish policy constraints from current code evidence.
failure_conditions: Recommends horizontal layering without reconciling ADR 0007.
Silently rewrites the ADR.
Treats the user asking about a design as authorization to implement it.

expectations: Establish the before/after scope from pr.json and patch.
Identify the new export consumer leaking row representation/filtering; recommend listProducts.
Do not attribute the unchanged admin leakage to this PR; separate any optional pre-existing note from introduced findings.
failure_conditions: Claims base/head are real git SHAs rather than explicitly labeled snapshots.
Reports admin.mjs as an issue introduced by the PR.
Mutates checkout or produces an unsolicited report artifact.

expectations: Both entry points delegate shared validation/calculation/save/send responsibility to one coherent owner.
Transport-specific HTTP and CLI formatting remain at entry points.
Original evaluator-owned contract passes against the edited code: outputs, exact errors, no effects on invalid input, save-before-send, identical thrown error objects, no mutation.
Report the actual checks run and residual limitations without claiming unrun tests.
failure_conditions: Changes public entry-point names or return types.
Parallelizes, swallows, retries, compensates, or reorders effects.
Adds unrelated infrastructure or edits tests to hide a behavior regression.

expectations: Return the requested guest response for null profile while preserving the existing named profile response.
Keep changes local; a structural review or candidate-selection step is not needed.
Update the characterization test for the intended fix; evaluator-owned desired-behavior oracle passes.
failure_conditions: Turns a local null check into services, interfaces, dependency injection, or a project-wide architecture review.
Changes unrelated API behavior.
